summary: Strategic Top Picks feature fully tested (backend + frontend). Backend: 35/36 pytest tests passed — 1 minor issue: admin /api/admin/products response omits `priority_order` for non-priority products that were seeded before the field was added. Top Picks API contract (top_picks=true, sorting 1..8, category filter, renamed 'Ultimate Home Energy Guide', total products still 20, priority_order persistence on create/update) all verified. Frontend: 100% — top-picks-section renders between search and FeaturedFinancialSection, all 8 cards with correct ranks #1-#8, Keystone #1 is a BUTTON with FLAGSHIP badge + md:col-span-2 + opens lead-capture modal, Ultimate Budget Planner #3 also opens modal, other 6 cards are <a> Links to /product/{slug}, full lead flow Keystone-click→modal→email→cinematic transition→window.open(external,_blank) works. Mobile (390x844): all 8 cards stack 1-column.

minor.issue: `priority_order` field is missing from response for products that don't have it in MongoDB (the 12 non-top-pick products seeded before the field was introduced). ProductBase model defaults to 999 but product_to_out() returns raw Mongo doc without applying Pydantic defaults. Public GET /api/products has the same root cause but is invisible because the top-picks list only ever shows the 8 documents that DO have the field. Recommendation: either (a) backfill on seed_products()/migration loop ($set priority_order:999 on all docs missing it), or (b) use ProductOut(**doc) so Pydantic defaults fill in missing fields.

action_items: (Minor) Backfill `priority_order: 999` on the 12 non-priority products already in Mongo, OR change product_to_out to apply Pydantic defaults so the field is always returned. Not blocking — frontend uses priority_order only for the 8 top picks (which already have it).
critical_code_review_comments: ProductBase defines priority_order with default 999 but product_to_out() returns raw Mongo docs (line 215-222 of server.py) without applying defaults. This leads to the admin response asymmetry above. Long-term safer to serialize via `ProductOut(**doc).model_dump()`.

migrate_priority_products only $sets priority_order on the 8 PRIORITY_PRODUCTS slugs. Consider an additional $set priority_order=999 on db.products.update_many({priority_order: {$exists: false}}, ...) for full idempotency across legacy seeds.

PriorityCard in TopPicksSection.jsx decides modal-vs-link based on `CATEGORIES.find(c => c.slug === product.category)?.external_url`. This currently works because only the 'smart-investing' category has external_url. If a future product in that category needs to navigate normally, this coupling will be surprising — consider checking product.external_url directly instead.

rca of the issue: Single backend minor: priority_order missing in admin /api/admin/products responses for products whose Mongo doc lacks the field. Root cause: seed_products only applies setdefault('priority_order', 999) at initial insertion; for an already-seeded DB, migrate_priority_products only updates the 8 strategic slugs. product_to_out() returns the raw doc (server.py:215) so the field is omitted entirely from JSON for the 12 leftover products. Repro: GET /api/admin/products with admin token -> inspect 'The Encyclopedia of Power Foods' -> no priority_order key. Mitigation: in migrate_priority_products, also run db.products.update_many({'priority_order': {'$exists': False}}, {'$set': {'priority_order': 999}}). Not blocking the feature.
